parsed.basis: Seychelles decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2016 and its 2024 Penal Code amendment adds gender identity to protected characteristics with enhanced penalties for hate-motivated violent offences, while the constitution prohibits torture and guarantees equal protection on grounds including sex. There is no criminal offence for being transgender, cross-dressing or presenting inconsistently with documents, and no documented programme of police targeting, facility bans or border refusal directed at transgender visitors. Anse aux Pins, a residential district south of Victoria on Mahé, has no separate local ordinance, enforcement practice or tourism-specific exception; visitors encounter the same national border, policing and health systems as elsewhere in Seychelles, in a small, tourism-oriented island society.
